turns.doctor_question: Hello. I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in to see me today?
turns.patient_response:
Hi, Dr. Smith. It's really nice to meet you. Um... I hope I'm in the right place, and I want to do whatever is helpful, so I'll just try to explain. 

I don't want to sound, you know, unreasonable or anything. But I'm here because for months now, I’ve just been trying to get people to understand what's going on with my husband’s family. They’ve been... well, they're quietly messing with our money and our good name. 

It's just these subtle things, you know? Like, I'm a billing clerk, and these little billing errors will suddenly just show up at work. Or someone at our church will just act really funny or cold toward me out of nowhere. And I know people probably think I'm making a fuss—they'll pull up all these records and try to explain it away—but I know it ties back to his family. I just know it does. 

I just really need someone to see what's happening. Does... does that make sense? Is it okay that I'm sharing this with you?

symptom_reasoning.S019: The patient expresses a fixed belief that her husband's family is sabotaging her finances and reputation, maintaining this conviction even when presented with contradictory records.

But... even when they show me those papers, I just... I know in my heart what's really happening. No matter what records anyone pulls up or how they try to explain it, I know it still ties back to his family. They are just so careful about it, you know? They know how to quietly mess with our money and our good name so that it *looks* like a normal mistake on paper. 

I'm sorry, I know that probably sounds so stubborn of me, and I really want to be cooperative with you. I hope you're not frustrated with me for saying that. I just have to be honest about what I know is happening... is it okay that I feel that way?
